ulysses.title: Library & sheets
ulysses.summary: Everything is a sheet in a three-pane library (groups, sheet list, editor). A line that starts with ? runs an agent and the answer is written into the same sheet as plain prose, so a chat and a note are the same object. Branches attach to marked passages, glued sheets form a manuscript whose headings are the outline, and [[links]] plus keywords populate a References view.

variants.label: Prose, margin branches
variants.summary: Questions and answers read as one continuous text with markup in the margin; branches are numbered margin notes beside the marked passage.

variants.label: Chat bubbles
variants.summary: Questions render as right-aligned bubbles under a sheet title; answers stay plain prose; everything else matches A.

variants.label: Branches as attachments
variants.summary: Branches leave the margin and are listed as attached sheets in the open attachments panel; passages keep a numbered marker.

variants.label: Two panes
variants.summary: The library collapses into a group menu above the sheet list and the attachments panel stays open, which leaves more room on small screens.

variants.label: Outline first
variants.summary: Opens on the Chapter 3 manuscript in Outline view; chats are reached from outline rows rather than from the sheet list.

macos.title: Mac system app
macos.influence: Apple macOS system app idioms (HIG; Finder, Mail, Messages, Freeform, System Settings)
macos.summary: Session becomes a standard Mac document app: a glass sidebar of folders, one toolbar view switch (Page, Outline, Columns, Map) over the same library, and an inspector (⌥⌘I) that holds a chat's branches and links. Chats read like Messages, notes are collapsible outlines with [[links]], and the first window offers one field — ask a question — with the agent check done in the background.

variants.label: Page + inspector
variants.summary: Opens on a chat in Page view with a Mail-style item list and an inspector holding Info, Branches and Links.

variants.label: Column browser
variants.summary: Opens in Columns view: folders → items → branches and bullets → Quick Look preview, replacing the column strip.

variants.label: Outline list
variants.summary: Opens in Outline view: one disclosure-triangle list of folders, chats, branches and note bullets; Space opens Quick Look.

variants.label: Popover branches
variants.summary: No inspector by default; numbered passage markers open branches in popovers, with an opaque, denser sidebar.

variants.label: Map canvas
variants.summary: Opens on a canvas map of chats, notes, highlights and links grouped by folder; the inspector follows the selected card.

notes.title: Notes with Ask
notes.summary: Session becomes a three-pane notes app: folders, a dated note list, and a note whose first line is its title. Any note can run a model inline (⌘J); answers stay in the note as editable text, and selecting a passage branches it into a linked sub-note. Outline and Link Map are two more views of the same notes, so there is one object to learn.

variants.label: Inline chats
variants.summary: Chats run as blocks inside the note; branches nest as sub-notes in the list; Linked Notes sits at the bottom of each note.

variants.label: Chat side panel
variants.summary: The note holds only the answer text; the conversation (questions, run status, follow-up box) lives in a panel beside it.

variants.label: Replies section
variants.summary: Branches do not appear in the note list; they are numbered on the passage and listed in a Replies section at the end of the note.

variants.label: Gallery home
variants.summary: Folders open in gallery view with run status on each thumbnail; Quick Note is the primary capture path.

variants.label: Link inspector
variants.summary: A right-hand inspector shows a mini link map, backlinks and tags for the open note; the tag browser shows counts.

notion.title: Pages & blocks
notion.summary: Everything is a page made of blocks: a chat is a page whose blocks are questions and answers, a note is a page you write, and a branch is a sub-chat nested under the passage it came from. One sidebar tree, @-links with backlinks, a Questions database (table/board/list/gallery) and a link map replace folders, feeds and three save gestures. First run opens a Getting started page with a single Ask box; agent setup is a non-blocking checklist item.

variants.label: Chat pages
variants.summary: Chats are pages in the tree; branches are sub-chat pages listed under the passage they came from; first run lands on Getting started.

variants.label: Questions database
variants.summary: Every chat is a row in a Questions database with Status, Agent and Model properties; the database is the landing view and chat pages show their properties.

variants.label: Branches as toggles
variants.summary: Sub-chats render inline as toggle blocks under the passage instead of separate pages, so one investigation reads as one page.

variants.label: Side peek
variants.summary: Outline-first: the Chapter 3 note is the landing page and chats open in a side peek beside it, keeping the note in view.

variants.label: Inline AI blocks
variants.summary: Questions are asked from an inline AI block at the end of any page; the chat composer is a block in the page flow rather than a docked bar.

inbox.title: Research inbox
inbox.influence: Front / Missive / Superhuman / Hey (shared email inbox apps)
inbox.summary: Every question is a Conversation that runs in the background and lands in an Inbox as “Ready to read”; queued and running ones sit in Waiting. Follow-ups are Ask replies, your own writing is a Note (the internal-comment idiom), and a passage can start a Fork. Tags, [[links]], backlinks and a Knowledge view with outline and graph replace folders, stars, bookmarks and the feed, so the first screen has one action: ask.

variants.label: Triage inbox
variants.summary: Three panes: mailboxes, one list per mailbox (Inbox, Waiting, Done), conversation, and a details sidebar with links and forks.

variants.label: Split inbox
variants.summary: The Inbox list is split into Ready to read, Waiting and Read sections, so running work is visible without switching mailboxes.

variants.label: Compose-first home
variants.summary: Inbox opens on a New conversation pane with suggestions from your notes, and the list has an inline quick-ask box.

variants.label: Notes in sidebar
variants.summary: No separate Knowledge view: notes and the outline open in a sidebar tab beside the conversation; the graph opens as an overlay.

variants.label: Compact, keyboard
variants.summary: Single-line rows, details sidebar closed by default, and a persistent shortcut bar for j/k, e, s, r, n, f triage.

tana.title: Everything is a node
tana.influence: Tana (with nods to Roam Research, Logseq, Workflowy)
tana.summary: Chats and notes live in one outline. A question is a node tagged #question: ⌘↵ runs it, the answer arrives as child nodes, follow-ups are child questions, and a selected passage becomes a #claim node that can be referenced anywhere. Home is today's page with one input line (⌘↵ asks, ↵ saves a note), so there is one first action and one place where everything lands.

variants.label: Prose answers
variants.summary: Answers arrive as one node per paragraph, tag fields render inline, and references are listed at the bottom of each page.

variants.label: Claim answers
variants.summary: The same answer is split into #claim nodes grouped under topic nodes, each with its source shown beside it.

variants.label: Fields as table
variants.summary: Tag fields render as a bordered field table, and live searches inside the outline render as tables.

variants.label: Workspace home
variants.summary: Home is the workspace outline instead of today's page, and the sidebar shows the outline tree instead of pins.

variants.label: References panel
variants.summary: A persistent side panel shows references and a local map for the current node, and bullets carry reference counts.

linear.title: Questions & Notes
linear.summary: Every investigation is a Question with one visible status (Queued, Running, Ready, Reviewed) and an agent as its assignee; sub-questions replace branches, Notes are outline documents, and Links are typed connections you can list or graph. One dense, keyboard-first list replaces the mixed chat-and-feed Home, so the first action is always the same: press C and ask.

variants.label: List + document
variants.summary: Home is a status-grouped list; a question opens as a document with sub-questions and an activity log below the answer.

variants.label: Board home
variants.summary: Home is a status board (Queued, Running, Ready, Reviewed) instead of a grouped list; the question page is unchanged.

variants.label: Conversation page
variants.summary: The question page is chat-centric: question, answers, follow-ups and run events read as one timeline, with sub-questions inline as events.

variants.label: Peek split
variants.summary: Clicking a row opens a docked preview beside the list (triage-style); Enter or double-click opens the full page.

variants.label: Links as graph
variants.summary: Links render as a graph: the question sidebar shows a local mini-graph, and the Links view opens on the workspace graph.
